open_points.subject: service-token operation rights
open_points.text: State 0 permits 'read a project' and 'list projects' to a trusted service whose token allows `personal_data`, and permits 'list rooms' and 'list artifacts' to a trusted service; A09 gives several such services `personal_data` but omits those operations from their rows, while saying every omitted operation is refused.
open_points.question: Do the operation rows in A09 override the generic trusted-service permissions in State 0, or must every service with the stated class receive those generic operations?
options: A09's rows are exhaustive and override the generic State 0 wording
State 0's generic permissions supplement each A09 row
Revise the rows or State 0 so they agree operation by operation

open_points.subject: failure precedence inside an A04 stage
open_points.text: A04 says "the first failure is its answer" and orders stages (1) through (6), but it does not order multiple checks within stage (4) or within stage (6).
open_points.question: When two checks in the same stage fail, which failure is the answer?
options: Define a total order for every check within each stage
Return a combined validation failure for same-stage failures
Permit any same-stage failure to win
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed, documented order within each stage.

open_points.subject: simultaneous owner sign-ins
open_points.text: The owner "receives an owner session" at sign-in, but A13 does not say whether another successful sign-in may coexist with it or ends an earlier owner session.
open_points.question: May the one owner have multiple live owner sessions at once?
options: Allow multiple independent sessions
A new sign-in ends every earlier owner session
Refuse a new sign-in while one session is live

open_points.subject: owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: The cookie is "only to Registry's own origin", but no Domain, Path, SameSite, host-only, or local-HTTP versus Secure-cookie behavior is stated; browser cookies are not scoped by full origin including port.
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes and host/path scope enforce the intended boundary, including access on the production host and HTTPS access from another machine?
options: Specify a host-only, interface-path, HttpOnly, SameSite and Secure policy
Use a host-wide cookie and rely on Registry ignoring it outside owner-interface routes
Require HTTPS for every owner-interface access so Secure is unconditional
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie restricted to the owner-interface path, with Secure whenever HTTPS is used.

open_points.subject: time of owner-session validity checking
open_points.text: A13 defines when a session is valid but does not say whether expiry is tested at request receipt, authentication, transaction start or commit.
open_points.question: Can an owner request authenticated just before the absolute or idle deadline commit after the deadline, or must the session still be valid when the action commits?
options: Validity at authentication is sufficient for that request
Validity must also hold at commit
All owner requests are serialized with expiry as a transition
open_points.default_guess: Accept a request if the session is valid when authentication is checked.

open_points.subject: concurrent updates of OwnerSession runtime facts
open_points.text: M11 now carries "the instant of its last request", at most one pending confirmation and at most one uploaded import file, while A13 and A16 serialize only narrower operations and do not order all concurrent requests in one owner session.
open_points.question: How are two concurrent requests in one owner session ordered when they update the idle instant, replace a confirmation, replace a file, or confirm while an upload is replacing the file?
options: Serialize every request that mutates one OwnerSession
Use atomic compare-and-set rules for each session fact
Allow races with whichever write commits last
open_points.default_guess: Serialize all mutations of one OwnerSession and keep `last_request` at the maximum request instant.

open_points.subject: audit sequence instance-mark durability
open_points.text: A15 says Registry records a number in the instance marks before the change commits, but does not state that this update is atomic and durably persisted before the store transaction can commit.
open_points.question: What crash-safe protocol guarantees that a committed audit entry can never have a number higher than the durable instance mark, and that a torn mark cannot cause reuse?
options: Atomically replace and durably sync the mark before committing the store transaction
Keep the allocator in another transactional durable store
Weaken the guarantee across crashes
open_points.default_guess: Atomically replace and fsync the mark and its directory before allowing the store commit.

open_points.subject: audit numbering after loss of instance marks
open_points.text: M09 now says a sequence number is "never reused, also after ... the store is restored", while A15 says loss of the marks together with a restore "could lower the numbering" and places that case outside Registry's guarantees.
open_points.question: Is non-reuse after every restore an unconditional model invariant, or is restore after loss of the instance marks an explicit exception?
options: Make the M09 invariant conditional on the instance marks surviving
Provide another durable source that preserves the unconditional invariant
Refuse any restore when the marks are missing
open_points.default_guess: Make survival of the instance marks a stated precondition of the restore guarantee.

open_points.subject: scope of import mapping errors
open_points.text: A16 rule 1 says the mapping shows "every malformed record and every id that conflicts", while rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects are "neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported".
open_points.question: Are malformed records and conflicts reported for the whole uploaded file or only for the selected projects and their records?
options: Only selected projects and their reachable records are checked and reported
The whole file is checked and reported before selection
Parse-level defects are global but domain conflicts are selection-scoped
open_points.default_guess: Check and report only selected projects and their reachable records, except defects that prevent parsing the file at all.

open_points.subject: duplicate project ids and project selection
open_points.text: A16 checks only picked projects, yet declares an id malformed when it occurs twice among records of one kind; it does not say how the owner can pick one project when two project records carry the same id.
open_points.question: How is selection defined when the mapping contains duplicate project ids, and does such a duplicate invalidate the file before picks can be interpreted?
options: Duplicate project ids make the whole file malformed immediately
Projects are selected by record occurrence rather than id
Selecting either occurrence brings both into the checked set and refuses them
open_points.default_guess: Treat duplicate project ids as a whole-file structural error before selection.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: The confirmation, migration closure and audit entry identify the uploaded file by "its digest", but no digest algorithm or definition of the digested bytes is given.
open_points.question: Which collision-resistant algorithm is used, and is the digest over the exact uploaded bytes or over a canonical parsed representation?
options: A fixed release-declared digest over exact uploaded bytes
A fixed digest over a canonical parsed representation
A State 6 field selects or declares the digest algorithm
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-fixed SHA-256 digest over the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: configuration mode without service tokens
open_points.text: A17 rule 1 permits an owner-only start with none of the four service tokens, but required test 1 says "A configuration without Client Portal's token stops the start" without limiting that result to a partially populated service-token set.
open_points.question: Does a configuration with no Client Portal token start owner-only when all four tokens are absent, and fail only when some but not all service tokens are present?
options: All four tokens or none is valid; every partial set fails
All four tokens are always required
An explicit owner-only mode flag distinguishes intentional absence
open_points.default_guess: Accept exactly all four or none, and interpret the test as a partial-set test.

open_points.subject: store and backup location separation
open_points.text: A17 validates that each location is usable but does not forbid the store location, backup location and instance-marks path from being equal, nested or aliased to the same filesystem object.
open_points.question: Which overlapping or aliased location layouts must startup refuse to prevent backup retention or temporary-file cleanup from affecting the live store or instance marks?
options: Require disjoint canonical paths and refuse nesting or aliasing
Allow nesting but reserve and protect named files
Permit any usable layout and make every file operation discriminate by format
open_points.default_guess: Require canonical, non-overlapping store and backup locations and reserve the marks file separately.

open_points.subject: backup cryptographic format
open_points.text: A18 requires backups to be encrypted and records a digest of their key, but specifies no authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce rules, key derivation, format authentication or digest algorithm.
open_points.question: What exact cryptographic construction makes a backup confidential and detects tampering or use of the wrong key?
options: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption format and fixed key-digest algorithm
Delegate the complete format to the fixed store backend
Require confidentiality only and rely on the restored store integrity check for tampering
open_points.default_guess: Define a versioned AEAD backup format with a fresh random nonce and a fixed collision-resistant key identifier.

open_points.subject: restore during the post-import backup window
open_points.text: A16 keeps pre-import backups until a backup containing the migration closure passes its check; during that interval A18 still permits the owner to restore a kept backup, but does not forbid choosing a pre-import backup.
open_points.question: What happens if production must be restored before the first checked post-import backup has replaced the pre-import recovery set?
options: Forbid restoring a pre-import backup once import committed
Allow it and require a controlled re-import or closure reconstruction
Synchronously obtain a checked backup before reporting the import accepted
open_points.default_guess: Mark pre-import backups ineligible for production restore as soon as the import commits, even before their eventual deletion.

open_points.subject: pre-import backups after deletion failure
open_points.text: M10 now says that once a backup holding the closure has passed its check, "no backup without it is kept"; A18 says backup deletion may fail, Registry keeps serving and deletion is retried later.
open_points.question: Does the M10 condition become true when the post-import backup passes its check or only after every pre-import backup has actually been deleted?
options: Only after all pre-import deletions succeed
Immediately after the check, making a deletion failure fatal or service-blocking
Allow old backups to remain but mark them unusable rather than "kept"
open_points.default_guess: Treat the condition as achieved only after all pre-import backups are deleted or durably marked ineligible for restore.

open_points.subject: post-restore retention reconciliation
open_points.text: A18 requires the owner to restore first in owner-only mode and reapply current erasure, restriction, relationship and audit-retention state before enabling tokens, while also saying Registry "cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done".
open_points.question: What prevents service tokens from being configured and Registry restarted before the required reconciliation is complete?
options: Accept this solely as an external owner procedure with no Registry guarantee
Store an enforced restore-pending marker cleared by an explicit owner completion action
Require a separately generated reconciled store before normal startup
open_points.default_guess: Add a durable restore-pending gate that blocks service-token startup until the owner explicitly completes reconciliation.

open_points.subject: security review status after the A19 change
open_points.text: A21 rule 2 says "A change to a decision a category names reopens this review"; the injection and browser categories name A19, and A19 has changed, but A21 still says the review is complete and `PERFORMED`.
open_points.question: Has the changed A19 been re-reviewed under every A21 category that references it, or is A21 currently reopened?
options: Reperform the affected review categories and record the new result
Mark A21 reopened until that review occurs
Declare the A19 change non-material and state why rule 2 does not apply
open_points.default_guess: Mark A21 reopened and reperform the injection and browser-boundary categories.

open_points.subject: uploaded import-file isolation and retrieval
open_points.text: A21 says the files/artifacts category answers "path ownership, never executed, storage isolation, who may retrieve it" by reference to A16, but A16 only says the file is kept in an owner session and never in the store; it does not say whether it is memory-backed or a temporary file, who owns any path, its permissions, or whether any operation can retrieve its contents.
open_points.question: What storage, ownership, permission, cleanup and retrieval rules apply to an uploaded import file while its owner session keeps it?
options: Keep it only in memory and expose no retrieval operation
Keep it in a private per-session temporary file with specified permissions and atomic cleanup
Permit backend-chosen temporary storage under a general isolation invariant
open_points.default_guess: Use a private per-session temporary file readable only by Registry, never expose a download, and delete it atomically when replaced or the session ends.
